sections.section_title: 1. Background: GLP‑1 Receptor Agonists and Immune‑Mediated Necrotizing Myopathy
sections.description: This section establishes the pharmacologic and clinical landscape of GLP‑1 receptor agonists, their known skeletal muscle adverse effects, and an overview of immune‑mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM) including its histologic hallmarks, autoantibody associations, and the concept of drug‑induced autoimmunity.
subtopics: Pharmacology and indications of GLP‑1 receptor agonists (semaglutide, tirzepatide)
Reported skeletal muscle adverse events: weight loss, rhabdomyolysis
Definition and histopathologic features of IMNM (necrosis, paucity of lymphocytic infiltrates)
Autoantibody profile: HMGCR, SRP, and other myositis antibodies
Seronegative IMNM: prevalence and diagnostic challenges
Mechanisms of drug‑induced autoimmunity (hapten, molecular mimicry, epitope spreading)
WHO‑Uppsala Monitoring Centre causality assessment framework for drug adverse events

sections.description: Chronological description of the patient’s journey from the initial semaglutide dose, through the acute adverse event, to the gradual development of proximal muscle weakness and dysphagia, along with a detailed physical examination.
subtopics: Patient demographics and comorbidities: obesity, NAFLD, hypertension, hypothyroidism, remote DVT/PE
Semaglutide administration and immediate reaction: nausea, vomiting, acute renal failure, metabolic acidosis
Initial laboratory values: CK 337 U/L, mild transaminase elevation, normal troponin
Four‑month progression: inability to sit/stand, dysphagia, dysphonia
Proximal muscle strength assessment on admission: quadriceps, deltoids, hip abductors
Absence of cutaneous, joint, or extra‑muscular manifestations

sections.section_title: 3. Diagnostic Evaluation: Laboratory, Imaging, and Histopathology
sections.description: Comprehensive review of all investigations performed, interpretation of results, and how they led to a definitive diagnosis of IMNM while excluding other causes.
subtopics: Serial creatine kinase trend (peak 3992 U/L), AST/ALT elevation due to hepatic steatosis
Thyroid and autoantibody panels: negative ANA, anti‑SSA/SSB, Jo‑1, SRP, HMGCR, etc.; SS‑B elevated at 2.4
Inflammatory markers: ESR 22 mm/h, CRP 22.8 mg/L
Cardiac biomarkers: troponin 62 pg/mL, pro‑BNP 4358 pg/mL and imaging findings
Imaging studies: femoral MRI (symmetric muscular oedema), cardiac MRI (myocardial oedema), echocardiogram, CT chest, abdominal ultrasound
Muscle biopsy findings: necrotic/regenerating fibres, CD68+ macrophages, acid phosphatase activity, C5b‑9 deposition, sparse CD3+ T cells
Liver biopsy confirming steatosis (NAFLD activity grade 5/8) and exclusion of hepatic myopathy
Differential process: exclusion of statin‑induced myopathy, drug‑induced rhabdomyolysis, polymyositis, inclusion body myositis, myasthenia gravis, thyroid myopathy

sections.description: Describes the pharmacologic interventions employed, the evidence and reasoning behind each therapeutic choice, monitoring strategies, and the eventual successful weaning off immunosuppression.
subtopics: High‑dose intravenous methylprednisolone pulse (1000 mg/day for 5 days) and expected corticosteroid response
Transition to oral prednisone 1 mg/kg/day and taper protocol
Indication for intravenous immunoglobulin: 2 g/kg over 4 days in severe cases
Monitoring of CK reduction, muscle strength, and potential steroid side effects
Role of GLP‑1 RA cessation and patient education to prevent rechallenge
Management of complications: pseudomonal septic shock, urinary tract infection
Follow‑up schedule: outpatient visits, CK monitoring, functional assessment

sections.description: Summarizes the patient’s recovery trajectory, normalisation of laboratory and imaging findings, and discusses the broader significance for clinical practice and pharmacovigilance.
subtopics: Ten‑month follow‑up: return to baseline functional status, off prednisone for 8 months
Sustained CK normalization and lack of relapse
Resolution of cardiac MRI abnormalities and stable echocardiogram findings
Application of WHO‑UMC criteria: probable causality between semaglutide and IMNM
Clinical teaching points: early recognition of drug‑induced myopathy, comprehensive workup, prompt initiation of immunosuppression
Potential pathogenic mechanisms of semaglutide‑induced autoimmunity
Future research directions: larger case series, predisposing factors, safety monitoring in GLP‑1 RA therapy
Take‑home lessons for clinicians managing patients on GLP‑1 receptor agonists
